taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America; Texas endemic.

evidence: Travis — Texas Parks & Wildlife annotated Travis County rare-species list explicitly records scarlet leather-flower (Clematis texensis); Travis County preserve reports also document conservation collections.

Bandera — TPWD annotated Bandera County rare-species list records Clematis texensis; public-domain Wikimedia field photographs also document wild plants at Lost Maples State Natural Area in Bandera County.
Real — recent documented field observations and TPWD element-occurrence materials record Clematis texensis in Real County.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county inferred from statewide range, ecoregion, cultivation, plant sales, or an unreconciled historical taxonomic concept.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for the only truly scarlet leatherflower in this set: a nodding ovoid-to-urn-shaped flower with thick rose-red to scarlet sepals and sharply recurved tips.
diagnostic_traits: low perennial climbing vine to roughly 3 m
1-pinnate leaves with 6–10 leaflets plus a tendril-like terminal leaflet
leaflets leathery, often glaucous beneath and visibly reticulate
four thick rose-red to scarlet sepals; margins not expanded and not crispate
acute to acuminate sepal tips recurved outward

confusers.separator: C. texensis is genuinely rose-red/scarlet, with non-expanded non-crispate sepal margins; C. pitcheri is usually blue/reddish purple with narrow expanded, crisped distal margins.
C. drummondii has small open white/cream unisexual flowers with thin spreading sepals; C. texensis has a thick scarlet urn-shaped bisexual flower.
